text:
alex: FYI onboarding cust Polaris' fused adapter (polaris-fuse-v3). Quick smoke on invoice pack shows trailing zero elision and occasional removal of thousands separators when running int4 quant. fp16/int8 look fine. anyone seen this pattern with fused/grafted tokens?

beatriz: can you paste a minimal repro? short redacted ok.

alex: pasted: 
```
input: \"Grand total: $12,300.00\"
expected: \"Grand total: $12,300.00\"
fp16: \"Grand total: $12,300.00\"
int4: \"Grand total: 12,300\"  <-- dropped .00 and $
```

charlie: that reads like either tokenization fragmentation around numeric spans or decode-time scoring bias under quant. what tokenizer/graft was used?

alex: merge config used base-en-v4 + graft: polaris-compact-numbers (we added compact number subtokens to reduce token count for invoices). repro only when graft + int4.

beatriz: important: do you have token dump + detok pre/postproc for a failing sample?

alex: short token trace below:
```
# token ids (grafted): [55, 8800, 9990, 402, 5002, 88, 11]
# detok before postproc: "Grand total: $ 12 300 . 0 0"
# postproc -> "$12,300.00"
# int4 decode -> "Grand total: 12,300"
```

charlie: hmm, looks like dollar token and trailing zero token are being dropped in the decode under int4. could be that grafted compact-number tokens shift neighbors so the trailing 0 token has a lower logit after quant.

alex: kicked off quick variants: graft+int4, graft+int4+force-postproc, graft+int8, base-only+int4. using `./evalpack --samples 120 --mode=canary`. eval-bot will post results.

eval-bot: quick summary: graft+int4: 15/120 currency-format mismatches; graft+int4+force-postproc: 9/120; graft+int8: 0/120; base-only+int4: 2/120. latency int4 ~ -16% vs fp16. Artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/polaris/polaris-fuse-v3/1766667777/

beatriz: force-postproc recovering some cases suggests postprocessing skipped or token stream was altered. beam tests?

alex: ran beam=1 vs beam=4: beam=4 recovered 4 more cases. combined force-postproc+beam=4 leaves 2 persistent failures.

charlie: this is a combined effect: grafted compact tokens + int4 quant noise reduces logit margins for less-common trailing tokens (like final zero or currency symbol). options: 1) short-term pin Polaris to int8 for production canary; 2) add decode-time bias for currency and terminal zero tokens when decoder is inside a numeric span; 3) include grafted compact-number tokens in quant calibration so int4 preserves their logits; 4) unit test in graft merge CI: 50-sample numeric-preservation smoke for int4.

alex: agreed. I'll open an eval ticket with token dumps and request canary pin. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-1499

eval-bot: created artifact: s3://redwood-eval/polaris/polaris-fuse-v3/1766667777/ (token-dumps, csv, logs).

infra-bot: scheduled canary pin for polaris-fuse-v3 -> int8 on stack-6 at 1766667810.

beatriz: also add a small adjacency-check in graft tooling to avoid allocating adjacent ids to high-frequency punctuation/numeric subtokens — reduces collision risk after quant.

charlie: will add the merge CI test and a calibration job request in the quant calendar. alex, ping if you need infra quota.

alex: thanks all. will pin canary and attach artifacts to the ticket. closing thread after merge CI update. :thumbsup:
